name: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
topics: Asymptotic Analysis and Loop Complexity
Discuss Big-O and Big-Omega notations and prove that ½n(n−1) = O(n²) by finding c and n₀.
Work out the time complexity of the given nested loops; which of the two given algorithms is better in the Big-O sense?
Recurrence Relations: Master Theorem and Recursion Tree
Solve the recurrences T(n) = 2T(√n) + log n and T(n) = 4T(n/2) + n²√n.
Solve T(n) = T(n/5) + T(4n/5) + n using the recursion tree method; compare algorithms A, B and C given by their recurrences.
Divide and Conquer: Sorting, Searching, Strassen
Apply Strassen's algorithm to the given matrices and analyse its complexity.

Design an O(log n) divide-and-conquer algorithm for the given search problem (index with T[i] = i / minimum of a decreasing-then-increasing array / missing term); analyse quick sort best and worst cases.
Greedy: Activity Selection, Fractional Knapsack, Scheduling
Compute a schedule with the maximum number of activities for the given start and finish times.
Solve the given knapsack instance with the greedy method; design a greedy algorithm to place songs on CDs or programs on a disk.
Huffman Coding
Construct the Huffman tree for the given characters and frequencies and calculate the total bits needed.
Explain the greedy Huffman coding algorithm, write its pseudocode and analyse its complexity.
Minimum Spanning Trees: Kruskal and Prim
Find the minimum spanning tree of the given graph using Kruskal's algorithm and analyse its complexity.
Do Prim's and Kruskal's algorithms work with negative edge weights? Does sorting edges in decreasing order give a maximum spanning tree?
Dynamic Programming: Matrix Chain, LCS, OBST, 0/1 Knapsack
Find an optimal parenthesisation of the matrix-chain product with the given dimensions.
Write the algorithm for the longest common subsequence and find the LCS of the given strings; construct an optimal binary search tree for the given probabilities.
Shortest Paths: Dijkstra, Bellman–Ford, Floyd–Warshall
Run the Bellman–Ford algorithm on the given graph from the source and show how it detects negative-weight cycles.
Solve the all-pairs shortest-path problem using Floyd–Warshall, showing D(k) after each iteration.
Graph Traversal and Topological Sort
Find the topological sort of the given DAG and how many topological orderings it has.
Show how DFS can be used to find strongly connected components; which DFS implementation is better for sparse graphs?
Backtracking and Branch and Bound
Explain the N-Queen problem and solve the 4/5-queen problem using backtracking with the state-space tree.
Compare backtracking with branch and bound; design a branch and bound algorithm for 0/1 knapsack.
String Matching: Naive, Rabin–Karp, KMP, Finite Automata
Explain the Rabin–Karp algorithm and find the spurious hits for the given text and pattern modulo q.
Using the KMP algorithm (or a string-matching automaton), search for the given pattern in the given text.
NP-Completeness and Reductions
Discuss the classes P, NP, NP-hard and NP-complete with a diagram, and the steps to prove a problem NP-complete.
Prove that the clique problem reduces to vertex cover / that set cover is NP-complete.
